question.text: The State of Lu's official chronicle, the Annals, provided the name for a "period" where the Eastern Zhou began named after two of these time periods-spring and autumn.
question.clue: To display the Emerald Buddha in Wat Phra Kaew, Rama I and Rama III constructed three sets of decorations based on these time periods, including a "rainy" example characterized by monsoons.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about dynasties of China.
swap.text: This last imperial dynasty of China was overthrown by the Xinhai ["sheen-hi"] Revolution. This dynasty fought the Opium Wars with Great Britain and the Sino-Japanese wars with Japan.
swap.clue: This dynasty's "century of humiliation" resulted after it was forced to sign a sequence of "unequal treaties'" marking its defeat in the Opium Wars.

question.leadin: This event's "Down to the Countryside" Movement sent youth from cities to farms, resulting in a "lost generation." --.
question.text: Identify this movement that targeted the "four olds." The "Gang of Four" became prominent during this period that attempted to purge any remaining elements of capitalism from a certain country.
question.clue: This period saw many "big-character" posters, the first of which was created by Nie Yuanzi, and the Four Olds were attacked, leading to the loss of many artifacts and historical records.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about stone constructions in China.
swap.text: The emperor Qin Shi Huangdi [chin shee hoo-ong dee] had this collection of thousands of clay sculptures built and buried with him.
swap.clue: According to the Records of the Grand Historian, flowing rivers of mercury were created near the site where these works were housed.

question.leadin: A system of law enforcement called baojia(BAO-jee-ah) was implemented during this dynasty by Wang Anshi (wong AN-shee).
question.text: Name this Chinese dynasty that invented gunpowder, which initially helped it fight off a Mongol invasion before it was replaced with the Yuan (YOO-un) Dynasty.
question.clue: Bi Sheng worked under this dynasty, which switched lines of succession due to the Jingkang Incident.

swap.leadin: After refusing to respond to Japanese incursions, this man was kidnapped by two subordinates and forced to ally with his political opponents in the Xi'an [shee an] Incident.
swap.text: Name this leader who reunified China during the Warlord Era.
swap.answerHtml: Chiang Kai-Shek [or Jiang Jieshi; or Chiang Chungcheng; prompt on partial answers that do not include the underlined portion]
swap.clue: This leader of the Northern Expedition was kidnapped by Zheng Xueliang in the Xi'an Incident.

question.leadin: Sir Halliday Macartney held this man hostage in a London embassy, which he described in the memoir Kidnapped in London.
question.text: Name this man who led the Xinhai revolution that toppled the Qing dynasty. This man served as the provisional first president of the Republic of China.
question.clue: Though he was educated in Hawaii, he was in exile in Japan when he formed the Tongmenghui society.

swap.text: The invasion was set off by this incident, in which Japanese military personnel framed China for plotting to blow up railroad lines owned by Japan.
swap.answerHtml: Mukden Incident [or September 18th incident; or Liutiaohu Incident; prompt on "Manchurian Incident"]
swap.clue: The Qing dynasty ended in 1912, though their last emperor-Puyi-became the puppet ruler of Manchukuo [man-choo-kwoh] after this 1931 incident in which a bomb went off near a railway controlled by Japan.

question.leadin: This founder of the state of Wei rose to prominence in the wake of Dong Zhuo's tyranny by defeating Yuan Shao at the Battle of Guandu.
question.text: Identify this Machiavellian strategist from Chinese history, who was ultimately defeated by Liu Bei at the Battle of Red Cliffs and died after Hua Tuo tried to combine cannabis and neural surgery.
question.clue: This man originally rose to power as a Chancellor of the Eastern Han dynasty in its waning days.

swap.text: This woman popularized the use of liangbatou ("liang-ba-TOE") headpieces to distinguish Manchu women from Han Chinese. This mother of the Tongzhi Emperor was the main power behind the throne during the late Qing dynasty.
swap.answerHtml: Empress Dowager Cíxǐ [or Empress Dowager T’zu-his; or Cíxǐ tàihòu; or Xitaihou; or Xiaoqin Xianhuanghou; prompt on Dowager Empress or Empress Dowager]
swap.clue: This leader, who was said to "rule from behind the curtains," developed the Beiyang fleet during the Self-Strengthening Movement.

question.text: The Sui Dynasty began the construction of this waterway connecting the Huang He and Huai rivers. Today, it connects Hangzhou and Beijing.
question.answerHtml: Grand Canal [or the Jing–Hang Grand Canal, or the Jīng-Háng Dà Yùnhé]
question.clue: In order to complete this project, the double slipway was replaced by the new pound lock.

swap.text: During World War I, Japan captured this city in Germany's Kiautschou Bay Concession. This Chinese city is home to St. Michael's Cathedral, built by German missionaries.
swap.clue: The German East Asia Squadron was previously based in this Chinese city, now in Shandong province. After von Spee and his fleet withdrew, the city was besieged by Japanese and British forces and fell in November 1914, with 1400 Allied casualties.

question.leadin: Answer the following about attempts to restore the Ming dynasty.
question.text: Resentment towards the succeeding Qing ("ching") dynasty came from the fact that their emperors were of this ethnicity. Their namesake region of China was turned into a Japanese puppet state during World War II.
question.clue: This group used Latin to write a treaty with Russia signed at Nerchinsk, rose to prominence under Nurhachi, and won at Shanhai Pass against Li Zicheng.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a Chinese dynasty.
swap.text: This dynasty, whose name translates as pure, survived the Boxer and Taiping Rebellions.

question.text: Amidst widespread instability and collapse of the monetary system, the Yuan ("ywen") dynasty was overthrown by these rebellions, an offshoot of the White Lotus movement.
question.answerHtml: Red Turban rebellions [or Hóngjīn Qǐyì; accept answers with synonyms for “rebellion”]

swap.text: The weakness of the later Western Han allowed this usurper to rule China as Xin emperor for about fifteen years, until his overthrow by the Red Eyebrows.
swap.clue: Flooding exacerbated tensions between this man's government and the peasantry, leading a faction called the Chimei ] to oppose him.

question.leadin: Name these people associated with the Manchu reign of China.
question.text: The Manchus took Beijing from this rebel who had seized the city from the last Ming emperor and proclaimed himself the first emperor of the Shun dynasty.

swap.text: An Lushan was assassinated by one of these people who An had made a eunuch. These people, who ruled the Liao Dynasty, founded a "black" state after a Jurchen invasion in 1124 forced them to flee to Central Asia.
swap.clue: The Goryeo Dynasty engaged in a series of wars with these Mongol barbarians. Ruled by the Liao Dynasty, they were based out of Manchuria and launched three major invasions of Korea.

question.leadin: Answer the following about "poet-historians" in Chinese history.
question.text: Du Fu is often considered one of the foremost poet-historians since his poems, such as "Lament by the Riverside," depict the sorrows of this political revolt instigated by a Sogdian, Turkic general.

swap.leadin: This format was invented by Wang Anshi, and first appeared around 1465.
swap.text: Name this specific form of "essay" that was required in order to pass the imperial examinations during the later Ming and Qing dynasties. Its rigid structure featured an opening, amplification, and then several arguments.
swap.clue: Imperial exam-takers wrote using this rigid essay format, which included a set number of sections and many formalized parallel sentences.
